info.title: Fleet Manager API
info.description: The public Fleet Manager control API. Mutations return durable operations; the controller-node channel is a separate, separately versioned protocol.

get.description:
This endpoint reads no state, requires no authorization, and creates no
operation. It exists so the conventions in this crate are exercised end to
end before any resource endpoint exists.

200.description: The API version this controller serves.

400.description: The supplied x-correlation-id header was not a canonical opaque Fleet identity.

ApiError.description:
The body of every unsuccessful response.

It is built from [`PublicError`], which is the type that decides what is
safe to disclose. Internal causes, provider output, and secret values are
excluded there rather than filtered here.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Clients branch on this, not on `message`.

correlationId.description:
The correlation identity of the request that failed. It is also returned
in the `x-correlation-id` response header, and is what an operator needs
to find the request in the audit trail.

fieldViolations.description: Per-field rejections, when the failure is a validation failure.

retry.description: Retry guidance for this specific failure.

FieldViolation.description: One rejected input, identified by its location in the request body or query.

code.description: Stable machine-readable reason this field was rejected.

field.description: JSON pointer into the request body, or a query parameter name.

Meta.description: Non-authoritative description of the API this controller serves.

apiVersion.description: The version segment of the served API path.

service.description: The service that answered, for operators reading a proxied response.

OperationAccepted.description:
What a mutation returns instead of holding the request open.

Per ADR-0002, a long infrastructure workflow is a durable operation the
caller polls or subscribes to, not an HTTP request kept alive for minutes.

correlationId.description:
Correlation identity shared by the request, the operation, and its audit
events.

operationId.description: Opaque identity of the durable operation.

status.description: The operation's state at the time the response was written.

OperationStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of a durable operation.

FM-108 owns the operation model itself. This enum exists so the accepted
envelope has a typed status from the start.

PageInfo.description:
Where a list response sits in its result set.

Pagination is cursor-based, never offset-based: an offset silently skips or
repeats rows when the underlying set changes between requests. The cursor is
opaque, and a client that parses one is relying on an implementation detail
that is free to change.

limit.description: The number of items this page was limited to.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page.

Resource_Meta.description:
A single resource.

The payload is nested under `data` so that later top-level fields are an
additive change rather than a breaking one.

data.description: Non-authoritative description of the API this controller serves.

Retry.description: Whether and how a caller may retry a failed request.
